browser_eval.rationale: The description says this tool `does NOT drive the browser itself`; it only `points you at agent-browser` and `tells you how to install it (if needed) and where to start`. Although the described CLI could later `open pages, click, type, screenshot, or capture console errors`, those actions are not advertised as actions performed by this MCP tool itself, so no SECRET/UNTRUSTED/SINK/HOSTEXEC label is assigned.

nextjs_docs.rationale: The tool is for `THIS project` and tells where docs are inside the locally installed package at `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`, and may determine whether `the project is on an older Next.js`. That is local project/package state, so it can return non-public host/project metadata into context. It `does NOT fetch documentation`, and the advertised output is local paths/instructions rather than attacker-authored web content, so UNTRUSTED and SINK are not assigned.

nextjs_index.rationale: The tool `Discover[s] all running Next.js development servers` and returns `Server port, PID, and URL` plus the `Complete list of available MCP tools` exposed by local dev servers at `/_next/mcp`. This is localhost/runtime project information, so it can return non-public local/server data. The discovered tool descriptions and schemas come from the running local Next.js server as advertised; the text does not show attacker-authored content or an attacker-readable destination.

nextjs_call.rationale: The tool can `Call a specific MCP tool on a running Next.js development server`. Common tools include `Error diagnostics`, `Route information`, and `Build status`, which can expose local app/runtime information, so SECRET applies. It can also invoke `Cache management (clear caches)`, making it state-changing. The advertised target is a local Next.js dev server identified by `port`; the description does not advertise requests to attacker-chosen external hosts, public posting, messaging, or host code execution. Because available tools `varies by Next.js version`, the exact downstream reach is not fully settled from the advertisement alone, but the least restrictive supported label from the text is SECRET and WRITE.

notes: No source code or output schemas were provided; output fields are inferred only from the advertised descriptions.
